sections.title: The letter ce
paragraphs: The letter is called (ce) /θe/. Its main sound is heard in the word (casa) /ˈka.sa/, which means house. This letter makes two different sounds in spoken Spanish.

sections.title: Mouth and voice
paragraphs: For the first sound, lift the back of your tongue to touch the roof. Block the air, then let it burst out. For the second sound, place your tongue tip between your teeth. Blow air through the narrow gap. Both sounds are voiceless. A voiceless sound means the voice is off, so your throat does not shake.

sections.title: When each sound occurs
paragraphs: The letter sounds like the first consonant in (casa) /ˈka.sa/ before a, o, u or consonants. You can also hear it in the word (clase) /ˈkla.se/. Before the letters e or i, it makes the sound heard in (cena) /ˈθe.na/. You also hear this softer sound in the word (cielo) /ˈθje.lo/.

sections.title: Common mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not release a puff of air with the first sound, like in English cat. Keep it crisp and dry. Before e or i, do not pronounce it like s in sun. Instead, use the sound of th in thing.
